title: Three truths
hook: Tiantai: emptiness, the provisional and the middle, all at once

segments.voice: Yesterday, Tiantai, the school on Zhiyi's mountain. Your line was the Lotus school. Did a detour find its place on the road? Today, one of that school's treasures. Day one thousand three hundred thirty-three.

Make a fist. Go on, either hand. There it is: a fist. Now open your fingers. Where did the fist go? It didn't fly off anywhere. There was never a fist apart from the hand curled up a certain way. And yet, a moment ago, it was a real fist. You could have knocked on a door with it. So which is true: there's no fist, or there's a fist? Tiantai's answer is yes. And then it adds a third thing. Tiantai calls them the three truths.
screen: `MAKE A FIST.` → `OPEN IT. WHERE DID IT GO?` → `NO FIST, OR A FIST?`

segments.voice: First, where it starts. A verse by the Indian teacher Nagarjuna, read in Chinese, says in substance: whatever arises from conditions, that is emptiness; it is a name given in dependence; and that is the middle way. Zhiyi read that one verse and heard three truths in it. Second, the three. Emptiness: the fist has no fist-ness of its own. It's made of a hand, a moment, a squeeze. Take those away and nothing is left over. The provisional: and still, the fist works. It has a name. It can knock. It's a real fist in the world of fists, even though it depends on everything else. The middle: the two aren't taking turns. The fist isn't empty on Monday and real on Tuesday. It is empty and real in the same instant, and the middle is simply that togetherness. Third, the turn Zhiyi gave it. Some teachers treated these as levels: first you see things as real, then you climb up to see them as empty, then, at the top, you see the middle. Tiantai calls that one way of teaching. Its own reading is that the three are perfectly joined. Each truth contains the other two. Look all the way into emptiness and the provisional world is right there. Look closely at the plain world and the middle is right there. Three, and at once. Fourth, what it changes. The school says this isn't a puzzle to win. It's a way of seeing a doorway, a quarrel, a face, without falling into either ditch: it's all nothing, or it's all solid. Tiantai keeps both feet on the road, and walks the middle of it.
screen: `NAGARJUNA'S VERSE, READ THREE WAYS.` · `EMPTY. PROVISIONAL. MIDDLE.` · `NOT LEVELS, BUT JOINED.` · `NEITHER DITCH.` · then, large: `THREE AT ONCE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: see one thing three ways. Pick something in front of you. A pen, a shoe, your own hand. First, look at it as empty: made of parts and causes, nothing in it that stands alone. A few breaths. Then look at it as provisional: it has a name, it does its job, it's really here. A few breaths. Then let both be true together, without choosing. Don't strain for a special feeling. Just keep the pen a pen and keep it empty at the same time, and breathe. The bell holds the time.
Three truths. Tiantai's teaching that every thing is empty, provisionally real, and the middle, all in one moment, each holding the others. Today's word.
Your line: three at once. Today, when something feels completely solid or completely pointless, look for the other two truths hiding in it. Day one thousand three hundred thirty-three.

howItsDone: Tiantai and Tendai Buddhists study the three truths, emptiness, the provisional and the middle, and use them as a way of contemplating any object or moment in meditation.

trapdoor: what you thought: three truths means three different facts to learn.
what it means: one thing seen as empty, as provisionally real, and as the middle, all in the same moment.
what a scholar hears: Zhiyi's reading of Nagarjuna's verse on emptiness, dependent naming and the middle way, with the three perfectly joined, not climbed as levels.

notes: Editor pass: cut the unsupported claim that Chinese readers turned the verse 'over and over' and a stock line in the hook; varied the hook's closing formula; swapped cup images for a doorway and a pen (cups recur on 1336, 1337, 1340); fork no longer puts the writer's fist illustration in Zhiyi's mouth.
Nagarjuna's verse (MMK 24:18) is paraphrased, following the Chinese (Kumarajiva) reading Zhiyi used; confirm the paraphrase.
The contrast between the three truths taught as sequential levels and as 'perfectly joined' (the separate vs. round teaching) is simplified; confirm it is fair to Tiantai's classification.
The fist image is the writer's illustration, not a traditional Tiantai example.
Original: 三諦, pronunciation sahn-DEE; confirm.
